summary: Global currency markets are navigating a firming U.S. dollar as traders position themselves ahead of the upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate decision. Risk sentiment remains carefully managed, with artificial intelligence jitters and corporate risk concerns driving intermittent safe-haven flows into the Japanese yen and keeping Treasury yields near recent lows. Meanwhile, regional currency movements reflect localized pressures, including political developments in Brazil and upcoming domestic budget releases in the UK.

Broad market sentiment is additionally influenced by safe-haven demand tied to declining Treasury yields and tech-sector jitters. Conversely, JPY maintains a net-long stance supported by safe-haven flows, while Gold exhibits an overwhelmingly bullish net-long position of nearly 200,000 contracts.

articles.title: Forex Daily Market Brief: Dollar Holds Firm and Yields Hover Ahead of Central Bank Decisions
articles.intro: Asian currencies mixed as the dollar holds firm and the yen retreats ahead of upcoming Federal Reserve decisions. Meanwhile, Treasury yields hover near three-week lows as AI jitters spur safe-haven demand.

sections.p: The broader market mood is characterized by cautious consolidation as participants weigh shifting fundamental pressures. Asian currencies remain mixed while the dollar rebounds and the euro slips ahead of key central bank decisions. At the same time, artificial intelligence jitters have spurred notable safe-haven bids, weighing on risk sentiment and driving Treasury yields toward their third consecutive weekly drop.

Macroeconomic attention is heavily focused on upcoming monetary policy events, including the Federal Reserve decision, Bank of Canada rate decisions, and the RBNZ Official Cash Rate statement projected alongside the Annual Budget Release for the UK. Market participants are closely monitoring these central bank trajectories while digesting secondary developments, such as Brazil's real weakening 12% following Lula's election victory and ongoing corporate technology headlines.

On the technical front, EUR/USD continues in a defined downtrend trading at 1.11881 with an RSI of 37.4, holding near support at 1.11771 and resistance at 1.1355. GBP/USD moves sideways at 1.33476 with an RSI of 59.6, bounded by support at 1.32008 and resistance at 1.34018. USD/CAD prints sideways at 1.4028 with an oversold RSI of 21.1, sitting between support at 1.3995 and resistance at 1.4262. Commitment of Traders data shows net positioning remaining heavily short on EUR at -134,524 contracts and GBP at -80,420 contracts, while USD Index net longs stand at 15,044 contracts.

Traders should look ahead to a busy economic calendar featuring upcoming Australian CPI data, New Zealand's Official Cash Rate announcements, and the critical central bank rate decisions from Canada and the United States. Keeping a close eye on these high-impact releases will be vital for assessing near-term volatility and liquidity shifts.
